workflows.helpLogicBehavior1: Logic nodes branch the flow based on a comparison, switch, or condition expression; each branch becomes an output port.

workflows.helpTriggerBehavior1: Trigger nodes start the workflow (HTTP webhook, schedule, container event, ...). Each workflow has exactly one trigger node.
workflows.helpTriggerBehavior2: HTTP triggers expose a secret that callers must include in the X-McHarbor-Trigger-Token header; the token rotates when you re-save the trigger.
workflows.helpUtilityBehavior1: Utility nodes transform, delay, or filter the msg payload between two operational nodes.

whatsNew.title: What's new in {{version}}
whatsNew.description: A quick tour of the latest changes.

selfProtection.title: Acting on McHarbor's own containers needs host_self.manage
selfProtection.description: Containers: on the environment McHarbor runs on, creating a container that mounts the host, joins another namespace or adds devices and capabilities, and restarting, stopping or restoring McHarbor's own containers, now also needs host_self.manage. Background runs on those containers are refused. Review roles that hold containers.manage or stacks.manage there.

rbacEnvScope.title: A role given on one environment no longer grants global keys
rbacEnvScope.description: Security → Users: a role assigned on one environment carries only that environment's keys, so users.manage, roles.manage, dashboard.view and the other global keys need a global assignment. Review your scoped roles.

setupToken.title: The installer asks for a setup token
setupToken.description: First-run installer: copy the one-time setup token into the Setup token field. The native installer prints it; otherwise read it from the McHarbor log (journalctl -u mcharbor on a native install, docker logs mcharbor in a container). It changes every time McHarbor restarts.

agentReleases.title: Agents update only from McHarbor
agentReleases.description: Agent installs and updates now come only from this McHarbor. Download and verify agent versions under Settings → Updates → Agents and pick the target; hosts never contact GitHub or a registry. Container agents need one reinstall from McHarbor.

csp.title: A Content-Security-Policy is now sent
csp.description: McHarbor now sends a Content-Security-Policy. If a third-party plugin misbehaves, set CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_REPORT_ONLY=true and check the browser console before relaxing it.

unsignedPlugins.title: Unsigned plugins need your explicit consent
unsignedPlugins.description: Installing or updating a plugin that no trusted key verifies now needs an explicit confirmation, and the server enforces it. Unsigned installs carry an Unsigned badge under App Store → Plugins.

gitopsWebhookSecret.title: GitOps webhooks now need a secret
gitopsWebhookSecret.description: A pull-request webhook was accepting unauthenticated requests: its signature check never ran. It now verifies an HMAC over the raw body against a per-repository secret, and a repository with no secret is refused. Generate one under GitOps → Repositories and set it on the forge, or deliveries return 401.

instanceBackup.title: Instance backup and restore
instanceBackup.description: Settings → System → Instance backup exports this whole instance into one encrypted file — roles, environments, secrets, the certificate authority your agents trust — on a schedule, to a storage location, with a restore rehearsal after each one. Restore it after losing the host, onto new hardware or another database, or restore just one category.

incidents.title: Incidents and AI narration
incidents.description: Incidents gathers a failing container's events, logs, deploys, audit trail, alerts and metrics on one screen, and the Virtual Machines, System Containers, Kubernetes and Swarm plugins now raise their own; turn on narration per environment under Incidents → Narration settings to have your AI model explain it, with the evidence for each cause.

reports.title: Sixteen more reports
reports.description: Reporting → Report Studio now covers incidents, drift, instance disaster recovery, high availability, ITSM tickets, approvals, secrets, workflows, webhooks and compliance, and the VM, system container, compute and log-forwarding plugins add reports on their own data.

ha.title: Active/passive high availability
ha.description: Run two nodes on PostgreSQL with one active; see every node and hand over or drain under Enterprise → High availability.

secrets.title: Secrets vault
secrets.description: Store a credential once under Security → Secrets and reference it as ${secret:NAME} from a stack, a container or a workflow. McHarbor substitutes it server-side when it calls Docker, and file mode keeps the value out of the container environment entirely.

credentialsAtRest.title: Stored credentials encrypted at rest
credentialsAtRest.description: On first boot after the upgrade, credentials saved before their column was encrypted — environment keys, agent tokens, registry and storage passwords, Kubernetes kubeconfigs — are encrypted in place. Snapshot driver secrets under Settings → Snapshots are now encrypted too and are no longer shown once saved: leave the field empty to keep the stored value.

database.title: PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB
database.description: SQLite is still the default, but McHarbor now runs on PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB as well. Settings → System → Database copies every row to the new backend and leaves the old one untouched as your rollback.

tls.title: HTTPS you can actually trust
tls.description: McHarbor is now its own certificate authority: a ten-year root signs a 90-day certificate and renews it without a restart. Download the root from Settings → Security → HTTPS, install it once per device, and the browser warning is gone. Remote agents pin that root automatically instead of skipping verification. Connections now negotiate TLS 1.3, the preferred floor McHarbor ships with. TLS 1.2 remains the minimum supported — set TLS_MIN_VERSION=1.2 if a client older than 2019 has to reach McHarbor.

hostUpdates.title: Host OS updates
hostUpdates.description: The environment page has an Updates tab: your host's distribution and kernel, a scheduled check for outstanding operating-system updates, and an apply that streams its output into the page. New in this build: “Install new packages when required” lets an upgrade install the image and header packages a kernel update needs — without it your kernel is reported as “kept back” and never applies. It is per environment and off by default, and it never removes a package.

pluginCatalog.title: Plugins come from the catalog
pluginCatalog.description: No plugin ships inside McHarbor any more. The Plugin Store downloads them from mcharbor.eu, which cuts the container image from 3.4 GB to about 760 MB. After this upgrade your installed plugins are re-downloaded automatically; anything that could not be fetched is listed under Settings → Plugins as Needs repair, with a Repair action.

plugins.title: Plugin platform
plugins.description: Kubernetes, Swarm, storage, communications, identity, scanners, and AI providers now ship as signed plugins you install from the Plugin Store.

compute.title: Virtual machines and containers
compute.description: Run KVM virtual machines and full-system LXC containers on your own hosts. Storage pools, host networking, verified guest images, browser consoles, snapshots and clones — with container limits that apply without a restart. Install the Virtual Machines or System Containers plugin to start.

rbac.title: Role-based access control
rbac.description: Roles, presets, per-environment and per-stack scopes, owner assignment, and temporary elevation gate every action. Denied controls stay visible and explain what is missing.

paletteSearch.title: Ctrl+K searches your plugins
paletteSearch.description: The command palette now lists the virtual machines, system containers, Swarm services, Kubernetes pods and compute hosts that installed plugins offer, and their actions such as creating a machine or adding a cluster, for the permissions you hold.

hostIo.title: Network and disk charts show live throughput
hostIo.description: Environments → an environment → Overview: Network and Disk I/O show bytes per second across the host's physical interfaces and disks, so traffic from containers, virtual machines and the host itself all counts.

vmHistory.title: Virtual machine charts open with the last hour
vmHistory.description: Virtual Machines → a machine → Overview: CPU, memory, disk and network charts start from a stored hour of samples and keep updating, and direct (macvlan) interfaces now report their traffic.

restoreUploadSelection.title: Restore from file lets you choose what to restore
restoreUploadSelection.description: Containers → a container → Backups → Restore from file: Read backup opens the archive first, then you pick its layers and files as for any other backup. Before, the whole archive was restored as soon as it was uploaded.

vmVaultSecrets.title: Take a VM's password and SSH keys from the vault
vmVaultSecrets.description: Virtual Machines → Create virtual machine → First-boot setup: From the vault picks the password, and SSH keys from the vault adds keys, by secret name (needs secrets.view). The value is copied once at create; rotating the secret later does not change the machine.

containerRestore.title: Restore a container with its configuration
containerRestore.description: Containers → a container → Backups → Restore: configuration can now be restored; the container is recreated with it, and the filesystem layer in the same restore is written into the new container. A ticked folder restores everything inside it.

accessibility.title: Clearer for screen readers and keyboards
accessibility.description: Status messages, option groups and progress bars are now announced by screen readers, every input is tied to its label, and a disabled button can still be focused so its tooltip tells you which permission it needs.

outboundGuards.title: Outbound fetches check the address first
outboundGuards.description: Catalog, image and cluster fetches now refuse loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses, and an https to http redirect. Kubernetes connections ignore HTTP_PROXY, catalogs on localhost need a LAN address, and the SQL Query node reads only the workflow tables. The LDAP plugin no longer accepts ldapi:// URLs. See Settings → Catalogs.
